description: Spellings of values and what a conforming reader does with each. integer, decimal, date, local-timestamp and offset-timestamp give the text of a string element in a column of that type, with the type parameters where the type has them. cells gives a JSON element of any kind in a column. quantize gives a decimal value, a target scale and a rounding mode, and the text of the value after quantization; value_changed and scale_changed say whether the cell counts toward the quantized and scale_changed counters. A refusal names the category and rule a conforming reader reports.

integer.note: The leading zero is reported before the sign of zero.
Grammar is judged before the type: negative zero, not a point mismatch.
38 significant digits: within the digit bound, so the type decides.
39 significant digits: the digit bound is judged before the type.

decimal.note: Grammar is judged before the type: a leading zero, not a scale mismatch.
Grammar is judged before the type: negative zero, not a scale mismatch.
39 significant digits: the digit bound is judged before the declared precision.

local-timestamp.note: A point with no digit is not a fraction of any width.
A comma is not a decimal point, so no fraction is present and what follows the seconds is not an offset. No timestamp column accepts this text.
A well-formed offset timestamp in a local-timestamp column: a mismatch with the schema, not malformed input.
The fraction fits; only the offset does not belong.
What follows the seconds is neither nothing nor an offset.
The date is judged before the time of day.
The time of day is judged before the fraction.
A malformed offset is invalid input in a column of either timestamp type.
Refused in every column, so not a value of the other type.
Well formed. The fraction width and the offset are both wrong for the column; the fraction is judged first.
Ten digits: well formed, and no column declares that width.
The malformed offset is judged before the width of the fraction.
The forbidden offset is judged before the absent fraction.
The calendar is judged before the kind of timestamp.
The clock is judged before the kind of timestamp.

offset-timestamp.note: Distinct from the same instant written with Z.
A well-formed local timestamp in an offset-timestamp column: a mismatch with the schema, not malformed input.
The fraction fits; only the offset is absent.
The fraction and the offset are both absent; the fraction is judged first.
The malformed offset is judged before the width of the fraction.
The forbidden offset is judged before the width of the fraction.
A point with no digit is not a fraction of any width.
The calendar is judged before the kind of timestamp.

cells.note: A string column keeps text that looks like a number.
A boolean is the JSON literal, never a string.
An empty string is not a null.

quantize.note: The target scale equals the declared scale: nothing changes.
The scale changes and the value does not.
A negative value that rounds to zero is written without a sign.
Two digits fit the declared precision of 2.
12.500 needs five digits and the declared precision is 3. Nothing is clipped.
